product.name: NexHub Building Management Sensor Hub Gen3
product.description: IoT gateway and sensor hub for smart building management systems. Aggregates data from up to 256 sensors (temperature, humidity, CO2, occupancy, energy metering) via Zigbee 3.0, Z-Wave, and Modbus RTU. Processes data locally on ARM Cortex-A53 and streams to cloud BMS platform via MQTT-over-TLS and REST API. Supports OTA firmware updates, remote configuration, and edge AI inference for anomaly detection. Deployed in commercial buildings, hospitals, and data centres across the EU.
product.intended_use: Building automation data aggregation and environmental monitoring. Intended for installation by certified building automation engineers in commercial, industrial, and healthcare facilities. Cloud connectivity used for remote monitoring, analytics, and OTA firmware delivery. Not intended for safety-critical building systems (fire, access control, life safety).

releases.release_notes: General availability release. Features: 256-sensor capacity, Zigbee 3.0 + Z-Wave LR + Modbus RTU, MQTT-over-TLS 1.3, REST API v2, OTA updates with A/B partition scheme, local edge AI inference (TFLite), Prometheus metrics endpoint, role-based web dashboard. Hardened Linux 6.1 LTS base with read-only root filesystem.

vulnerability_reports.title: Zigbee Stack: Touchlink Commissioning Without Authentication Enables Device Takeover
vulnerability_reports.description: The Zigbee 3.0 Touchlink commissioning channel (used for proximity-based device pairing) does not validate the initiating device's identity. Within radio range (~10m), an attacker can initiate a factory reset of paired Zigbee end devices by sending a Touchlink reset command. This causes sensor data loss and may trigger BMS alerts in monitored facilities. Discovered by NexConnected internal security research.

vulnerability_reports.title: REST API: JWT Token Validation Bypass via Algorithm Confusion (alg:none)
vulnerability_reports.description: The NexHub REST API v2 authentication middleware does not enforce a strict allowlist of accepted JWT signing algorithms. An attacker can forge a JWT token by setting the algorithm field to 'none', bypassing all cryptographic validation. Any unauthenticated client with network access to the API port (TCP 8443) can access any API endpoint with arbitrary claims, including admin-level configuration endpoints.

vulnerability_reports.title: OTA Update Handler: Firmware Signature Verification Time-of-Check Time-of-Use Race Condition
vulnerability_reports.description: The OTA update process verifies the firmware image signature before writing to the inactive A/B partition, but there is a TOCTOU window of approximately 200ms between signature verification and the start of the flash write operation. An attacker with control of the update delivery channel (e.g., compromised cloud update server or MitM on MQTT channel) could replace the verified image with a malicious one during this window.

vulnerability_reports.title: Prometheus Metrics Endpoint: Unauthenticated Exposure of Sensor Data and Device Topology
vulnerability_reports.description: The Prometheus metrics endpoint (TCP port 9090) is accessible without authentication by default and exposes detailed building sensor data including occupancy patterns, energy consumption, device inventory with MAC addresses and firmware versions. This can facilitate physical security attacks (identifying unoccupied rooms) and targeted follow-on technical attacks.

vulnerability_reports.title: Z-Wave LR: Denial of Service via Malformed S2 Security Frame
vulnerability_reports.description: A malformed Z-Wave S2 security encapsulated frame with an invalid length field in the nonce sub-command causes an assertion failure in the Z-Wave stack, crashing the sensor management daemon. The device automatically restarts (watchdog, ~45s recovery), but repeated attacks can render the hub non-functional. Affects all Z-Wave devices within radio range (~150m in LR mode).

security_advisories.title: Zigbee Touchlink Reset Vulnerability — Update to Firmware 3.1.0
security_advisories.summary: A vulnerability in the Zigbee 3.0 Touchlink commissioning implementation allows an unauthenticated attacker within radio range to reset paired Zigbee devices. Firmware 3.1.0 disables Touchlink by default and adds proximity confirmation requirements when enabled.
security_advisories.workaround: Disable Zigbee Touchlink commissioning in the hub web dashboard under Settings > Zigbee > Touchlink. This may require re-pairing sensors in close proximity during commissioning.
security_advisories.remediation_steps: Apply firmware 3.1.0 via OTA update (automatic if auto-update enabled) or manually via hub web dashboard Settings > Firmware Update. Verify update success in the system log.

security_advisories.title: CRITICAL: JWT Authentication Bypass — Immediate Update Required
security_advisories.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability in the NexHub REST API allows unauthenticated attackers to perform any API operation including reading sensor data, modifying configuration, and disabling security features. All NexHub Gen3 devices running firmware below 3.2.0 are affected. Immediate update is required.
security_advisories.workaround: If immediate update is not possible: (1) Restrict access to TCP port 8443 at the network perimeter to authorised IP addresses only. (2) Disable remote API access in hub network settings. (3) Monitor access logs for unexpected API activity. WARNING: Workaround does not protect devices on untrusted network segments.
security_advisories.remediation_steps: Apply firmware 3.2.0 immediately via OTA update. If auto-update was disabled, enable it temporarily or apply manually. After update, rotate all API credentials and review audit logs for evidence of exploitation. Report any suspected exploitation to NexConnected PSIRT at psirt@nexconnected.com.

security_updates.title: Firmware 3.1.0 — Zigbee Touchlink Hardening & Sensor Stack Updates
security_updates.description: Disables Zigbee Touchlink commissioning by default. When enabled, adds 30-second proximity window and confirmation dialog on hub touchscreen. Updates Silicon Labs EmberZNet SDK from 7.3.0 to 7.4.2. Adds Z-Wave S2 frame length validation. Minor fix for Modbus RTU timeout handling.
security_updates.integrity_info: SHA-256: 2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824. Signed by NexConnected Firmware Signing Key (RSA-4096, key ID: 0xNCS2024). Signature verifiable via /api/v2/ota/verify endpoint.

security_updates.title: Firmware 3.2.0 — JWT Authentication Fix (CRITICAL)
security_updates.description: Rewrites JWT validation middleware to enforce strict algorithm allowlist (RS256 only). Removes algorithm negotiation from token headers. Migrates all API tokens to RS256 signed with 4096-bit keys. Invalidates all existing sessions on update — all API clients must re-authenticate. Also includes: Python jose library replaced with custom implementation, OpenSSL 3.3.2, mosquitto 2.0.20.
security_updates.integrity_info: SHA-256: 9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08. Emergency signing by NexConnected PSIRT using HSM-protected key. Signature chain verifiable at https://nexconnected.com/security/fw-signatures/3.2.0.

security_updates.title: Firmware 3.2.1 — Prometheus Endpoint Authentication + OTA TOCTOU Fix
security_updates.description: Enables authentication on Prometheus metrics endpoint (configurable: mTLS or Bearer token). Adds file descriptor lock between OTA signature verification and partition write to close TOCTOU window. Reduces OTA verification-to-write window from 200ms to under 1ms. Also hardens OTA channel to reject firmware not delivered over MQTT with valid server certificate.
security_updates.integrity_info: SHA-256: b14a7b8059d9c055954c92674ce60032c0b7c08f7d99f9ced43ccc27f3c3e. Signed NexConnected Firmware Signing Key RSA-4096.

sbom_records.notes: Full system SBOM generated from production OTA image. Includes all Python packages from virtual environment. Z-Wave and Zigbee SDKs are third-party proprietary components — version provenance verified against silicon vendor release notes. SBOM published to customers via Product Portal for their own vulnerability tracking.
SPDX format generated for customers using SPDX-compatible toolchains. Same component inventory as CycloneDX SBOM. Provided for interoperability with EU CRA SBOM submission tooling.

Delta SBOM for firmware 3.2.1 — lists only components that changed versus the 3.0.0 baseline SBOM. Use in conjunction with the baseline SBOM to reconstruct the full component inventory for version 3.2.1.

risk_assessments.title: NexHub BMS Gen3 — Full CRA Cybersecurity Risk Assessment
risk_assessments.methodology: STRIDE threat modelling per OWASP IoT Attack Surface Areas. Attack surface enumeration per ENISA Good Practices for IoT Security. CVSS 3.1 scoring. Privacy impact assessment performed in parallel (GDPR — occupancy data is personal data under CJEU Planet49 precedent). Remote processing element threat analysis per CRA Article 6.
risk_assessments.summary: Seven attack surfaces identified across wireless radio interfaces (Zigbee, Z-Wave), network APIs (REST, MQTT, Prometheus), OTA update mechanism, and cloud integration channel. Three critical risks identified pre-release — all mitigated prior to market launch. Post-launch, two critical vulnerabilities (Zigbee Touchlink, JWT bypass) identified and resolved. Two high-severity items currently in remediation (OTA TOCTOU, Z-Wave DoS). Cloud remote processing element introduces data sovereignty risks addressed via EU data residency commitment.

risk_items.title: REST API Authentication Bypass
risk_items.description: Flawed JWT validation allows unauthenticated access to all API endpoints, enabling attackers to read occupancy data (privacy violation), modify building control settings, disable security features, or trigger firmware rollback to a vulnerable version.
risk_items.threat_scenario: External attacker discovers the NexHub device's IP address (e.g., via Shodan) and sends a crafted request with a JWT signed with algorithm 'none'. Attacker gains full API access, extracts occupancy schedules for a hospital, and disables intrusion detection sensor reporting.
risk_items.asset_affected: REST API, all sensor data, device configuration, firmware update mechanism
risk_items.mitigation_plan: 1. Enforce strict JWT algorithm allowlist (RS256 only) — implemented in firmware 3.2.0. 2. Remove algorithm field from JWT token headers (server-side algorithm only). 3. Rotate all API credentials on update. 4. Implement IP-based rate limiting on API endpoint. 5. Add anomaly detection for unusual API activity patterns.

risk_items.title: OTA Firmware Update — Supply Chain Attack via Compromised Update Server
risk_items.description: If the NexConnected cloud update infrastructure is compromised, or if a MitM is positioned on the MQTT channel, a malicious firmware image could be delivered to devices. The TOCTOU race in the OTA handler could allow substitution of a verified image after signature check.
risk_items.threat_scenario: Nation-state attacker compromises NexConnected's update delivery infrastructure. Malicious firmware is pushed to 50,000+ deployed devices simultaneously via the OTA channel, creating a botnet or disabling building management systems across multiple facilities.
risk_items.asset_affected: OTA update mechanism, all deployed devices, cloud update infrastructure
risk_items.mitigation_plan: 1. Close TOCTOU window with file descriptor lock (firmware 3.2.1). 2. Implement code signing with HSM-protected key. 3. Certificate pinning for update server. 4. A/B partition scheme limits blast radius to one boot slot. 5. Automatic rollback if post-update health check fails. 6. Canary deployment — update 1% of devices before fleet-wide rollout. 7. Rate-limit OTA pushes and alert on unusual fleet-wide update patterns.

risk_items.title: Privacy Violation — Occupancy Data Exposure via Unauthenticated Prometheus Endpoint
risk_items.description: Building occupancy patterns inferred from motion and CO2 sensor data constitute personal data under GDPR. Unauthenticated access to the Prometheus metrics endpoint exposes this data, violating GDPR Article 5 and CRA security requirements simultaneously.
risk_items.threat_scenario: A tenant in a multi-occupant commercial building scans the local network, discovers the NexHub Prometheus endpoint on port 9090, and scrapes occupancy data for all office zones. Data is used for competitive intelligence or sold to third parties.
risk_items.asset_affected: Prometheus metrics endpoint, building occupancy data (personal data), GDPR compliance
risk_items.mitigation_plan: 1. Require authentication on Prometheus endpoint (mTLS or Bearer) — firmware 3.2.1. 2. Default firewall rules block port 9090 to external network interfaces. 3. Privacy-preserving metrics: aggregate/anonymise occupancy data before exposure. 4. GDPR DPIA completed and documented. 5. Data minimisation: only expose metrics strictly needed for BMS operations.

risk_items.title: Cloud Remote Processing — Data Sovereignty and Availability Risk
risk_items.description: Sensor data streamed to the NexConnected cloud platform (hosted on AWS eu-west-1) is subject to cloud provider availability risks and potential government data access requests. Healthcare facility customers may have strict data residency requirements.
risk_items.threat_scenario: AWS eu-west-1 region outage causes loss of BMS visibility for all connected buildings simultaneously. Hospital facility manager loses remote monitoring capability during a critical HVAC failure event.
risk_items.asset_affected: Cloud platform, MQTT streaming, remote monitoring capability, data residency compliance
risk_items.mitigation_plan: 1. Local data retention for 30 days on-device regardless of cloud connectivity. 2. MQTT reconnect with exponential backoff and local buffer. 3. On-premise deployment option for healthcare customers (NexHub Private Cloud). 4. EU data residency commitment — all data processed in AWS eu-west-1 or eu-central-1. 5. Data processing agreement template aligned with GDPR Chapter V.

risk_items.title: Zigbee Network — Rogue Device Injection into Mesh Network
risk_items.description: A rogue Zigbee device in proximity of the hub can attempt to join the Zigbee network and inject false sensor readings (e.g., fake temperature spikes, false CO2 alarms) that trigger inappropriate BMS responses.
risk_items.threat_scenario: A malicious actor in a shared building carries a rogue Zigbee device programmed to inject false CO2 alarms, triggering automatic ventilation increases and disrupting the building's energy management.
risk_items.asset_affected: Zigbee mesh network, sensor data integrity, building control actions
risk_items.mitigation_plan: 1. Zigbee 3.0 network uses AES-128 link-layer encryption with unique network key. 2. Device allowlist — only pre-commissioned devices accepted. 3. Install-code-based commissioning for secure device onboarding. 4. Anomaly detection flags statistically implausible sensor readings. 5. Manual approval required for new device joins in secure mode.

risk_items.title: Z-Wave LR — Radio Denial of Service
risk_items.description: Malformed Z-Wave S2 security frames can crash the Z-Wave management daemon, causing hub restart and temporary loss of all Z-Wave sensor connectivity. Repeated attacks can render the Z-Wave network permanently unavailable without physical intervention.
risk_items.threat_scenario: Attacker within 150m of a building (e.g., from a car park) runs an automated script transmitting malformed Z-Wave frames continuously. Z-Wave sensors (including energy meters and heating controls) go offline, disrupting building management.
risk_items.asset_affected: Z-Wave radio interface, Z-Wave sensor network availability
risk_items.mitigation_plan: 1. Add S2 frame length validation before processing (in progress). 2. Watchdog timer ensures recovery within 45 seconds. 3. Sensor data cached locally — hub continues operating with cached readings during restart. 4. Radio interference detection and alerting. 5. Z-Wave network key rotation capability for suspected compromise.

cvd_policies.policy_text: NexConnected Systems operates a responsible vulnerability disclosure programme for all NexHub products. We request a 90-day coordinated disclosure window from the date of initial report. Given the IoT deployment context and OTA update timelines, we may request a one-time 30-day extension for complex vulnerabilities requiring hardware-validated patches. Our commitments: (1) Acknowledge within 24 hours; (2) Provide CVE ID within 10 business days if applicable; (3) Weekly status updates; (4) Credit researchers in our security advisory unless they prefer anonymity; (5) Hall of Fame recognition for valid reports. We operate a bug bounty programme through HackerOne for NexHub products. Payouts: Low €200, Medium €1000, High €3000, Critical €8000. We notify ENISA via the EU vulnerability database within 72 hours for actively exploited vulnerabilities per CRA Article 14. PGP fingerprint: A1B2 C3D4 E5F6 7890.

support_periods.justification_text: 5-year security update commitment for NexHub Gen3 product line. IoT devices in building management systems have typical deployment lifespans of 7-10 years. 5-year security support covers the primary deployment period. Extended support (to 2035) available via NexConnected Extended Care subscription at €50/device/year.
support_periods.expected_use_time_text: Building management IoT hardware is typically replaced at 7-10 year facility refresh cycles or when hardware performance becomes insufficient. 5-year software security support aligns with EU CRA baseline requirements and covers the highest-risk early deployment years when most vulnerabilities are discovered.
support_periods.comparable_products_text: Siemens SIMATIC IOT2050: 5-year security support. Advantech WISE-710: 5-year. Schneider Electric EcoStruxure: 7-year. NexConnected 5-year commitment aligns with lower end of market — Extended Care subscription available for longer assurance requirements.
support_periods.third_party_support_constraints_text: Support lifetime constrained by Silicon Labs EFR32MG21 Zigbee chipset support window (vendor committed to 2032). Z-Wave 700 series chipset (Silicon Labs ZGM130S) supported to 2033. ARM Cortex-A53 compute module support from SoC vendor until 2031.
support_periods.user_facing_summary: NexConnected provides security updates for NexHub BMS Gen3 devices until 15 January 2030. Updates are delivered automatically via OTA update (enabled by default) at no additional charge. Devices with auto-update disabled must be manually updated via the hub web dashboard.
support_periods.packaging_summary: Security updates until: 15 January 2030. Automatic OTA delivery. Free of charge.

certification_records.certification_scheme_label: ETSI EN 303 645 v2.1.1 — Consumer IoT Security
certification_records.scope_description: ETSI EN 303 645 v2.1.1 conformity assessment for NexHub BMS Gen3 (NEXHUB-BMS-G3) firmware v3.0.0. Assessment covers all 13 provisions: no universal default passwords, vulnerability disclosure policy, software update mechanisms, credential storage, communication security, minimised attack surface, software integrity, personal data protection, resilience, telemetry, opt-out for data sharing, device management deletion, and installation security.
certification_records.notes: Assessment completed with 1 deviation (Prometheus endpoint authentication — provision 5.6-1) accepted as non-conformance with remediation committed via CAP. Deviation resolved in firmware 3.2.1. Maintenance report pending SGS Brightsight review.

certification_records.scope_description: Zigbee 3.0 product certification for NexHub Gen3 Zigbee coordinator/router functionality. Covers Zigbee stack conformance, interoperability with certified end devices, and security key management per Zigbee 3.0 specification.
certification_records.notes: Certified by CSA through authorised test laboratory. Certificate maintained through firmware updates that do not modify the Zigbee radio stack. EmberZNet SDK update from 7.3.0 to 7.4.2 (firmware 3.1.0) confirmed compatible — re-certification not required per CSA maintenance procedure.
